message.content:
{
  "decision": "APPLY",
  "workflow_yaml": "name: .NET Build and Test

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - '**'
    tags-ignore:
      - '**'
  workflow_call:
  workflow_dispatch:

jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: windows-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      - name: Checkout sources
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0 # avoid shallow clone so nbgv can do its work.
          submodules: true

      - name: Setup .NET
        uses: actions/setup-dotnet@v6
        with:
          dotnet-version: 10.0.x

      - name: Cache NuGet packages
        uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: ~/.nuget/packages
          key: ${{ runner.os }}-nuget-${{ hashFiles('**/*.csproj', '**/*.sln') }}
          restore-keys: |
            ${{ runner.os }}-nuget-

      - name: Test
        run: dotnet test
",
  "rationale": "Two evidence-supported optimizations are applied: (1) Add NuGet package caching using actions/cache@v4, supported by the P-LIT-GHA-CACHE pattern and experiment showing ~6% elapsed time reduction for dependency caching. The cache key uses project files (*.csproj, *.sln) as inputs, satisfying the precondition that cache inputs include lockfiles. (2) Add a 10-minute job timeout (timeout-minutes: 10), supported by P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT and P-LIT-HISTORY-TIMEOUT patterns and experiments that add per-job timeouts to prevent runaway consumption. The timeout provides operational headroom for .NET build and test on windows-latest while bounding CI costs. Both changes preserve all build and test coverage and introduce no new permissions or network access.",
  "evidence_ids": [
    "experiment:batch-interactive-three--f6d2974a5cef7cc9",
    "pattern:P-LIT-GHA-CACHE",
    "experiment:batch-ishara-pattern-bat-a14b642d809bf336",
    "pattern:P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT"
  ]
}
